Study record: Reckon the Exodus month as the first month of the year
Form basis: "it shall be the first month" (12:2)

Study record: Slaughter the Passover at the prescribed time and location
Form basis: "shall slaughter it toward evening" (12:6)

Study record: Do not eat the Passover animal raw or boiled
Form basis: "You shall eat none of it raw" (12:9)
Note: Mixed: the verse also requires roasting ('but roasted with fire'); main clause, per title and 613 match N125, is the ban on eating it raw or boiled.

Study record: Do not leave Passover meat until morning
Form basis: "You shall leave none of it until morning" (12:10)
Note: Exodus 12:10 prohibits leaving the meat overnight. Its conditional requirement to burn any remainder has its own catalogue record, C0100, so this overnight ban is a single negative provision.

Study record: Do not break a bone of the Passover
Form basis: "you shall not break a bone of it" (12:10)

Study record: Keep the Passover memorial throughout the generations
Form basis: "You shall celebrate it as a feast" (12:14)

Study record: Eat unleavened bread during the appointed seven days
Form basis: "For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread" (12:15)
Note: Not mixed: the leaven removal and leaven-eating ban in this verse are separate records (C0109, C0106).

Study record: Do not eat leaven during the seven-day feast
Form basis: "whoever eats leaven … that soul shall be destroyed" (12:15)

Study record: Hold the appointed holy assemblies on the first and seventh days of Unleavened Bread
Form basis: "The first day shall be called holy" (12:16)
Note: Not mixed: the work ban in the same verse is recorded separately (C0108).

Study record: Do no prohibited work on the first and seventh days, with the stated food exception
Form basis: "You shall do no servile work on them" (12:16)
Note: Not mixed: besides the work ban the verse adds only a permission (food preparation); the P 613 matches (rest) match the holy-day clause recorded in C0107.

Study record: Remove leaven from Israelite houses for the seven-day feast
Form basis: "you shall remove leaven out of your houses" (12:15)
Note: Mixed: 12:19 adds the prohibition 'no leaven shall be found in your houses' (N201); main clause, per title, is the duty to remove leaven (P156).

Study record: Observe the Passover night as a vigil for the Lord
Form basis: "a vigil for the Lord … throughout their generations" (12:42)

Study record: Apply the stated circumcision and participation rules for the Passover meal
Form basis: "No uncircumcised person shall eat of it" (12:48)
Note: Mixed: verses 44 and 48 also require circumcising slaves and a foreigner's males before they eat; main clause is the eating ban on outsiders and the uncircumcised.

Study record: Keep the Passover meat within the house where it is eaten
Form basis: "shall not take any … meat outside the house" (12:46)
Note: Mixed: also 'It shall be eaten in one house' (requirement); main clause, per title and 613 match N123, is the ban on taking meat outside.

Study record: Apply the same prescribed law to native and resident foreigner
Form basis: "There shall be one law for the native" (12:49)
Note: Exodus 12:43–49 limits the parity rule to Passover, and verse 48 specifies circumcision before a resident foreigner participates. The feast determines the primary category and equal legal treatment supplies the Civil aspect.
Adjudication: Independent category audit · Scripture review resolved

Study record: Consecrate the firstborn males to God
Form basis: "Consecrate to Me every firstborn" (13:2)
Note: Covers human and animal firstborn; area follows the firstborn given to God (613 match P79). Redemption of sons is recorded separately (C0119).

Study record: Keep all leaven out of sight within your borders for the seven days
Form basis: "no leavened thing shall be seen with you" (13:7)
Note: Not mixed: the verse's 'eat unleavened bread' clause is a separate direction, as the context note says.

Study record: Redeem the firstborn donkey as prescribed
Form basis: "you shall exchange for a sheep" (13:13)
Note: The firstborn donkey is redeemed, not offered on the altar, so the area follows redemption rather than offerings.

Study record: Redeem firstborn sons
Form basis: "Every firstborn of man … you shall redeem" (13:13)

Study record: Keep the seventh day as a holy Sabbath rest
Form basis: "Tomorrow is a Sabbath, a holy rest" (16:23)
Note: Exodus 16:23 calls the seventh day a holy rest and verse 26 confirms the recurring schedule. The manna directions explain the occasion. Exodus 20:8–11 and Deuteronomy 5:12 support the weekly-rest label under the rubric.

Study record: Have no other gods
Form basis: "You shall have no other gods" (20:3)

Study record: Do not make idols or images for worship
Form basis: "You shall not make for yourself an idol" (20:4)

Study record: Do not bow down to other gods
Form basis: "You shall not bow down to them" (20:5)

Study record: Do not serve other gods
Form basis: "neither shall you serve them" (20:5)

Study record: Do not misuse God's name
Form basis: "You shall not take the name … in vain" (20:7)

Study record: Do ordinary work in six days and rest on the seventh
Form basis: "You shall do no work on it" (20:10)
Note: Mixed: 'For six days you shall labour' frames the schedule; the operative rest clause is the work ban (N320), so Negative.

Study record: Honour father and mother
Form basis: "Honour your father and your mother" (20:12)

Study record: Do not commit adultery
Form basis: "You shall not commit adultery" (20:13)

Study record: Do not steal
Form basis: "You shall not steal" (20:14)

Study record: Do not murder
Form basis: "You shall not murder" (20:15)

Study record: Do not bear false witness against your neighbour
Form basis: "You shall not bear false witness" (20:16)

Study record: Do not covet your neighbour's wife
Form basis: "You shall not covet your neighbour’s wife" (20:17)

Study record: Do not covet your neighbour's possessions
Form basis: "You shall not covet your neighbour’s house" (20:17)

Study record: Do not build God's stone altar with hewn stones
Form basis: "you shall not build with hewn stones" (20:25)

Study record: Do not ascend the altar by steps exposing nakedness
Form basis: "You shall not go up by steps" (20:26)

Study record: Release the Hebrew servant after six years under the stated household conditions
Form basis: "he shall go out free, without payment" (21:2)

Study record: A Hebrew servant may choose to remain under the prescribed procedure
Form basis: "His master shall pierce his ear" (21:6)
Note: The servant elects to stay in Exodus 21:5. Verse 6 requires his master, the record’s stated audience, to present him at the tribunal and pierce his ear. The procedure is mandatory once the choice is made.

Study record: Provide redemption for the betrothed servant woman rejected by her master
Form basis: "he shall redeem her" (21:8)
Note: Not mixed: the ban on selling her to foreigners (21:8) is recorded separately (C0167).

Study record: Do not sell the rejected servant woman to foreigners
Form basis: "he has no right to sell her" (21:8)
Note: Exodus 21:8 expressly removes the master’s right to sell the woman to a foreign nation. The protection is a Civil limit on sale with a Moral aspect stated in the master’s breach of faith.

Study record: Treat a servant woman betrothed to the master's son according to a daughter's rights
Form basis: "he shall deal with her … for daughters" (21:9)

Study record: Do not deprive the servant wife of her necessities
Form basis: "he shall not deprive her of her necessities" (21:10)

Study record: Do not deprive the wife of her clothing
Form basis: "he shall not deprive her … her clothing" (21:10)

Study record: Do not deprive the wife of conjugal companionship
Form basis: "he shall not deprive her … conjugal companionship" (21:10)

Study record: Release the servant wife without payment when her stated rights are withheld
Form basis: "she shall go out freely, without silver" (21:11)

Study record: Remove the deliberate murderer from sanctuary protection for judgment
Form basis: "you shall take him from My altar" (21:14)

Study record: Execute the person who strikes father or mother
Form basis: court penalty: "shall surely be put to death" (21:15)
Note: Exodus 21:15 imposes a death penalty for striking a parent. The catalogue records the legal consequence as Positive and Civil. Maimonides N319 enumerates the underlying prohibition on striking a parent.

Study record: Apply the prescribed death judgment for reviling father or mother
Form basis: court penalty: "shall surely die" (21:16)
Note: Exodus 21:16 imposes death for reviling a parent, as does the parallel in Leviticus 20:9. The catalogue records the legal consequence as Positive and Civil. Maimonides N318 enumerates the underlying prohibition.

Study record: Execute the kidnapper who enslaves or sells the victim
Form basis: court penalty: "he shall surely die" (21:17)

Study record: Compensate the injured person's lost labour and healing costs
Form basis: "he shall pay for his lost labour" (21:19)

Study record: Apply the stated judgment when a master fatally beats a slave
Form basis: court penalty: "he shall surely be avenged by judgment" (21:20)
Note: Not mixed: 21:21's 'he shall not be avenged' limits the penalty rather than forbidding an act.

Study record: Impose the assessed fine for the pregnancy injury described in this verse
Form basis: "he shall surely be fined" (21:22)

Study record: Apply the prescribed proportionate life-and-injury judgment
Form basis: "he shall give life for life" (21:23)

Study record: Release the servant whose eye or tooth the master destroys
Form basis: "he shall set them free for their eye" (21:26)

Study record: Stone the ox that fatally gores a person
Form basis: court penalty: "the bull shall surely be stoned" (21:28)
Note: Not mixed: the ban on eating the ox's flesh (21:28) is recorded separately (C0183).

Study record: Do not eat the flesh of the condemned goring ox
Form basis: "its flesh shall not be eaten" (21:28)
Note: Exodus 21:28 expressly bars eating the ox’s flesh. The selected provision governs consumption, which fits Dietary laws. Its application only after the fatal goring and condemnation establishes the Civil overlap.

Study record: Apply the negligent owner's death liability or imposed ransom for a known dangerous ox
Form basis: court penalty: "its owner also shall die" (21:29)
Note: Owner's culpable negligence after warning makes the death a capital wrong, so Moral second; the rule itself is court liability.

Study record: Pay the prescribed compensation when an ox kills a slave
Form basis: "he shall give thirty didrachmas of silver" (21:32)

Study record: Compensate the owner of an animal lost in an uncovered pit
Form basis: "the owner of the pit shall make restitution" (21:34)

Study record: Settle loss caused by an ox killing another ox, distinguishing prior knowledge of danger
Form basis: "they shall sell the living bull and divide" (21:35)

Study record: Make the prescribed restitution for stolen property, with the stated multiples
Form basis: "he shall repay five calves for the calf" (21:37)

Study record: Distinguish the stated night and daylight liabilities when a burglar is killed
Form basis: status rule: "he is guilty; he shall die in return" (22:2)

Study record: Sell the thief unable to pay the required restitution
Form basis: court penalty: "let him be sold for the theft" (22:2)

Study record: Repay double when the stolen animal is found alive with the thief
Form basis: "he shall repay them double" (22:3)

Study record: Compensate for damage caused by grazing another person's field or vineyard
Form basis: "he shall repay from his own field" (22:4)

Study record: Compensate for fire damage caused to another person's crops or land
Form basis: "he who kindled the fire shall make restitution" (22:5)

Study record: A thief caught stealing entrusted goods repays double
Form basis: "he shall repay double" (22:6)

Study record: Require double restitution from the convicted party in the property dispute
Form basis: "Whoever is convicted … shall repay his neighbour double" (22:8)

Study record: Accept the keeper's exonerating oath without demanding restitution
Form basis: "The owner shall accept it" (22:10)
Note: Not mixed: 'he shall not make restitution' is an exemption from liability, not a prohibition.

Study record: Apply the keeper's restitution liability for theft and the exemption for proved wild-animal loss
Form basis: "he shall make restitution to its owner" (22:11)
Note: Not mixed: 'he shall not make restitution' (22:12) is an exemption from liability, not a prohibition.

Study record: Apply the stated borrower liability and owner-present or hire exceptions
Form basis: "he shall make restitution" (22:13)
Note: Not mixed: 'he shall not make restitution' (22:14) is an exemption from liability, not a prohibition.

Study record: Pay the prescribed marriage payment for seducing an unbetrothed virgin, subject to her father's refusal
Form basis: "he shall surely give the marriage payment" (22:15)

Study record: Execute the practitioner of sorcery
Form basis: court penalty: "You shall not preserve sorcerers alive" (22:17)
Note: A court penalty, but phrased as a prohibition ('shall not preserve … alive'); Negative per the operative words and 613 match N310.

Study record: Execute the person who has sexual relations with an animal
Form basis: court penalty: "you shall surely put to death" (22:18)

Study record: Apply the prescribed destruction to the person sacrificing to other gods
Form basis: court penalty: "shall surely be destroyed" (22:19)

Study record: Do not mistreat or oppress the resident foreigner
Form basis: "you shall not ill-treat a resident foreigner" (22:20)

Study record: Do not mistreat the widow or orphan
Form basis: "You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan" (22:21)

Study record: Do not press a poor borrower harshly
Form basis: "you shall not press him hard" (22:24)

Study record: Do not charge interest to a fellow Israelite
Form basis: "neither shall you lay interest upon him" (22:24)

Study record: Return the poor debtor's covering pledge by sunset
Form basis: "you shall restore it to him" (22:25)

Study record: Do not revile the 'gods' named in the Saints text
Form basis: "You shall not revile gods" (22:27)
Note: Exodus 22:27 clearly prohibits reviling, but the Saints wording ‘gods’ and the adjacent ruler clause leave the referent open. Acts 23:5 quotes the ruler clause. A judicial reading of the first clause would support Civil overlap.

Study record: Do not speak evil of the rulers of your people
Form basis: "neither shall you speak evil of the rulers" (22:27)

Study record: Do not delay the prescribed firstfruit offerings
Form basis: "You shall not delay the firstfruits" (22:28)
Note: Not mixed: the verse's second clause (give the firstborn of your sons) is a separate provision.

Study record: Give the firstborn animal to God on the eighth day, after seven days with its mother
Form basis: "on the eighth day you shall give it" (22:29)

Study record: Do not eat flesh torn by wild animals and throw it to the dogs
Form basis: "shall not eat flesh taken by wild animals" (22:30)
Note: Mixed: also 'throw it to the dog' (disposal directive); main clause, per 613 match N181, is the ban on eating torn flesh.

Study record: Do not accept or circulate a false report
Form basis: "You shall not receive an empty report" (23:1)

Study record: Do not follow the crowd into wrongdoing
Form basis: "You shall not join the many in evil" (23:2)
Note: 613 match P175 (majority rule) rests on a rabbinic reading; this verse's wording is wholly prohibitive, so not mixed.

Study record: Do not pervert justice
Form basis: "neither shall you … turn aside judgment" (23:2)
Note: This record selects the second clause in Exodus 23:2 about turning aside judgment. It governs witnesses or judgments as well as personal integrity, matching the Civil overlap used for judicial corruption in C0225.

Study record: Do not favour the poor in judgment
Form basis: "Neither shall you favour a poor man" (23:3)
Note: Exodus 23:3 expressly prohibits favoritism in judgment, so its judicial role is as explicit as the Moral/Civil counterpart against favoring the powerful in Leviticus 19:15 (C0611).

Study record: Return your enemy’s straying ox or beast of burden
Form basis: "you shall surely turn it back" (23:4)

Study record: Help raise an enemy’s animal fallen under its load
Form basis: "you shall raise it up together with him" (23:5)
Note: Mixed: also 'you shall not pass it by' (N270); main clause, per title, is the duty to raise the animal with its owner.

Study record: Do not pervert the justice due to the poor in his cause
Form basis: "You shall not pervert the judgment" (23:6)
Note: Exodus 23:6 concerns judgment of the poor in a specific legal cause, in addition to its moral duty of impartiality. Compare the Moral/Civil labels for the parallel prohibition on perverting judgment in Deuteronomy 24:17.

Study record: Keep away from a false accusation
Form basis: "shall keep far away from every unrighteous charge" (23:7)
Note: Exodus 23:7 directs the hearer to keep away from unjust charges in affirmative terms. The separate clauses about killing the innocent and acquitting for gifts establish the Civil context for that Moral duty.
Adjudication: Independent category audit · Scripture review resolved

Study record: Do not execute the innocent or righteous
Form basis: "the innocent … you shall not kill" (23:7)
Note: The Moral protection of innocent life also specifically limits Israel's judges and execution authorities in the catalogue and legal context of Exodus 23:7. Civil is a clear secondary category.

Study record: Do not accept bribes or acquit the guilty for gifts
Form basis: "you shall receive no gifts" (23:8)
Note: Bribe-taking and unjust acquittal are moral wrongs; addressed to those judging, so Civil second. 'Keep far away' is an avoidance duty, not a separate requirement.

Study record: Cultivate and gather the land's produce during the six working years
Form basis: "you shall sow your land" (23:10)
Note: Exodus 23:10 uses affirmative wording for sowing and gathering. Its contrast with the compulsory seventh-year release in verse 11 supports an allowance for ordinary cultivation. The language also permits a reading as a prescribed working-year pattern.

Study record: Let the land rest in the seventh year
Form basis: "you shall grant it release, and leave it" (23:11)
Note: Land rest is the sabbatical year's core observance, so Ceremonial second. N220 (no sowing) is implied by 'leave it', not stated, so not mixed.

Study record: Leave sabbatical-year produce available to the specified people and animals
Form basis: "leave it; and the poor … shall eat" (23:11)
Note: Produce left for the poor and wild beasts parallels the harvest provisions for the poor: Civil with Moral second.

Study record: Do not invoke the names of other gods
Form basis: "Do not call to mind … other gods" (23:13)
Note: 'Keep everything I have said' is a general exhortation, not a separate requirement, so not mixed.

Study record: Observe the three pilgrim feasts and the required appearances before God
Form basis: "you shall keep a feast to Me" (23:14)

Study record: Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread
Form basis: "Keep the feast of unleavened bread" (23:15)
Note: The verse's empty-handed clause is a separate record (C0232), so not mixed.

Study record: Do not appear before God empty-handed
Form basis: "You shall not appear before Me empty-handed" (23:15)
Note: Concerns the gift brought when appearing at the feasts, hence Sacrifice and offerings; the verse's feast-keeping clause is a separate record (C0231).

Study record: Keep the Feast of Harvest or Weeks
Form basis: "you shall keep the feast of harvest" (23:16)

Study record: Keep the Feast of Ingathering or Booths
Form basis: "you shall keep … the feast of completion" (23:16)

Study record: Do not offer the sacrificial blood with leaven
Form basis: "you shall not sacrifice … with leaven" (23:18)

Study record: Do not leave the feast's sacrificial fat until morning
Form basis: "neither shall the fat … remain until morning" (23:18)

Study record: Bring the firstfruits of the land to God's house
Form basis: "You shall bring the firstfruits" (23:19)
Note: 613 match N187 belongs to the verse's milk clause, a separate record (C0238), so not mixed.

Study record: Do not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk
Form basis: "You shall not boil a lamb" (23:19)
Note: The verse's firstfruits clause is a separate record (C0237), so not mixed.

Study record: Do not imitate the nations' idolatrous practices
Form basis: "nor do according to their works" (23:24)
Note: Exodus 23:24 records both a ban on imitating idolatry and a duty to destroy the cult objects. The latter has its own catalogue record, C0242, and belongs to the conquest setting. C0241 covers only the prohibition.

Study record: Make no covenant with the Canaanite peoples or their gods
Form basis: "You shall make no covenant with them" (23:32)
Note: Exodus 23:31–32 gives Israel a territorial context for the treaty prohibition, and Deuteronomy 7:1–2 repeats it for the peoples in the land. The express extension to their gods adds the Moral dimension.

Study record: Do not let the specified peoples remain in Israel’s land
Form basis: "neither shall they dwell in your land" (23:33)
Note: Exodus 23:33 prohibits the specified peoples from remaining in Israel’s land. Serving their gods is the stated danger of settlement, so the selected residence provision is Civil.

Study record: Supply pure beaten olive oil for the sanctuary light
Form basis: "to bring you pure beaten olive oil" (27:20)

Study record: Priests: maintain the sanctuary lamps from evening to morning
Form basis: "Aaron and his sons shall burn it" (27:21)

Study record: High priest: wear the sounding robe when ministering in the sanctuary
Form basis: "Aaron’s sound shall be heard when he ministers" (28:35)

Study record: Priests: wear the covering undergarments when entering or ministering
Form basis: "Aaron and his sons shall wear them" (28:43)

Study record: Give the appointed sacrificial portions to the priests
Form basis: priestly portion: "shall belong to Aaron and to his sons" (29:28)

Study record: Transfer the high priest's holy garments to his successor
Form basis: succession: "Aaron’s holy robe shall belong to his sons" (29:29)

Study record: Do not allow outsiders to eat the consecration meal
Form basis: "An outsider shall not eat them" (29:33)
Note: Exodus 29:33 requires the consecrated priests to eat and separately forbids outsiders to eat. C0329 records the outsider restriction. The positive duty addresses the priests.

Study record: Do not eat the consecration leftovers after the appointed time
Form basis: "it shall not be eaten" (29:34)
Note: C0331 forbids eating the leftovers in Exodus 29:34. Burning the remainder is a distinct positive duty and already has its own catalogue record, C0330.

Study record: Offer the daily morning and evening lambs with the prescribed grain, oil and wine
Form basis: "shall offer on the altar: two year-old lambs" (29:38)

Study record: Burn the prescribed incense morning and evening
Form basis: "Aaron shall burn finely ground compounded incense" (30:7)

Study record: Do not offer unauthorized incense on the incense altar
Form basis: "You shall not offer other incense" (30:9)

Study record: Do not use the incense altar for burnt or grain offerings
Form basis: "shall not offer … an offering, or a sacrifice" (30:9)

Study record: Do not pour libations on the incense altar
Form basis: "you shall not pour a libation on it" (30:9)

Study record: Make the annual blood purification of the incense altar
Form basis: "Once a year Aaron shall make expiation" (30:10)

Study record: Give the equal prescribed census ransom for each counted adult male
Form basis: "each shall give the Lord a ransom" (30:12)
Note: 'The rich shall give no more and the poor no less' fixes the equal amount within the duty; not a separate prohibition, so not mixed.

Study record: Priests: wash hands and feet before sanctuary entry or altar ministry
Form basis: "shall wash their hands and feet with water" (30:19)

Study record: Do not apply holy anointing oil to unauthorized persons
Form basis: "It shall not be applied to human flesh" (30:32)

Study record: Do not reproduce holy anointing oil for private use
Form basis: "you shall not make anything like it" (30:32)

Study record: Do not reproduce the holy incense for personal enjoyment
Form basis: "You shall not make incense for yourselves" (30:37)

Study record: Keep the Sabbaths as the lasting sign between God and Israel
Form basis: "See that you keep My Sabbaths" (31:13)
Note: Exodus 31:13 and 16 require Sabbath observance, and verse 17 ties it to the seventh day of creation. The weekly-rest rule is Moral under the rubric. Its express function as Israel’s covenant sign supports Ceremonial secondary.

Study record: Execute the Sabbath profaner under Israel's prescribed judgment
Form basis: court penalty: "shall surely be put to death" (31:14)
Note: Exodus 31:14–15 states the penalty for Sabbath profanation and work. Numbers 15:32–36 shows the congregation executing the penalty in an actual case. Civil describes the sanction and Moral reflects the weekly Sabbath under the rubric.

Study record: Do not kindle fire in your dwellings on the Sabbath
Form basis: "You shall not kindle a fire" (35:3)
Note: 613 match N322 is the rabbinic court-execution reading of this verse; the plain text forbids kindling fire. A detailed Sabbath rite, so Ceremonial per the tie-breaker.

Study record: Present a burnt offering of the prescribed eligible animals or birds
Form basis: "he shall bring an unblemished male" (1:3)

Study record: Prepare and present the grain offering in its prescribed form with oil and, where specified, frankincense
Form basis: "his gift shall be fine flour" (2:1)

Study record: Give the grain offering remainder to the eligible priests for eating in the holy place
Form basis: priestly portion: "what remains … shall be Aaron’s and his sons’" (2:3)

Study record: Do not make the altar grain offering with leaven
Form basis: "You shall not make with leaven any sacrifice" (2:11)

Study record: Do not burn honey on the altar
Form basis: "shall not be brought up upon the altar" (2:12)
Note: Leviticus 2:11 concerns leaven and honey generally. Verse 12 directly distinguishes the permitted firstfruits gift from putting it on the altar.

Study record: Leaven and honey may be brought as firstfruits
Form basis: "gift of firstfruits you shall bring them" (2:12)
Note: Leviticus 2:11–12 distinguishes altar restrictions from firstfruits. The context supports an exception allowing these ingredients, while verse 12’s affirmative wording can also prescribe bringing them as firstfruits. The passage gives no independent offering schedule for them.

Study record: Include the covenant salt with every offering
Form basis: "every gift … shall be seasoned with salt" (2:13)
Note: Also forbids omitting it: 'You shall not let the salt of the covenant … cease' (N99).

Study record: Prepare a first-produce grain offering with roasted groats, oil and frankincense
Form basis: "shall bring the sacrifice of the first produce" (2:14)

Study record: Present an unblemished animal of the prescribed kinds for a peace or deliverance offering
Form basis: "he shall bring it unblemished before the Lord" (3:1)

Study record: Do not eat the prohibited fat of cattle, sheep or goats
Form basis: "you shall eat neither any fat" (3:17)

Study record: Bring the prescribed sin offering for an inadvertent offence, according to the offender's standing
Form basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished calf" (4:3)

Study record: Disclose relevant testimony when solemnly called as a witness
Form basis: duty to testify: "if he does not declare it" (5:1)
Note: Guilt for withholding testimony makes testifying a duty, as P178 counts it; truthful witness is also a moral duty, so Moral second.

Study record: Confess the offense in the stated witness, impurity, or oath cases
Form basis: "he shall confess the sin" (5:5)
Note: Leviticus 5:5 directly requires confessing the specified fault. Numbers 5:6–7 also treats confession as a distinct duty. Leviticus 5:6 links it to atonement and supports the secondary Ceremonial label.

Study record: Bring the prescribed offering for the stated witness, impurity and oath offences, with poverty substitutions
Form basis: "he shall bring unto the Lord" (5:6)

Study record: Add neither oil nor frankincense to the flour sin offering
Form basis: "He shall pour no oil upon it" (5:11)
Note: The flour-bringing clause (5:11a) belongs to the sliding-scale offering with poverty substitutions (C0411); this record is the oil and frankincense ban, so not mixed.

Study record: Give the flour sin offering remainder to the priest
Form basis: priestly portion: "what remains shall be the priest’s" (5:13)

Study record: Bring the prescribed guilt ram for misuse of holy things
Form basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:15)

Study record: Repay misused holy property with an added fifth
Form basis: restitution: "he shall repay … and add a fifth part" (5:16)
Note: Leviticus 5:16 first requires repayment plus one fifth, then assigns the priest a distinct atonement duty. The recorded restitution is Civil, and the consecrated property being restored supplies its Ceremonial aspect.

Study record: Bring the prescribed guilt ram for the unrecognized offence
Form basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:18)

Study record: Restore the wrongfully retained property and add a fifth upon acknowledgment or conviction
Form basis: restitution: "he shall return the plunder which he seized" (5:23)
Note: Restitution for theft, fraud and false oath: Civil, with Moral second because the underlying acts are moral wrongs.

Study record: Bring the prescribed guilt ram for dishonest dealings and false oaths
Form basis: "he shall bring … an unblemished ram" (5:25)

Study record: Keep the altar fire burning continually without quenching it
Form basis: "fire of the altar shall burn upon it" (6:2)
Note: Also forbids quenching it: 'and shall not be quenched' (N81).

Study record: Do not bake the priests' grain offering portion with leaven
Form basis: "It shall not be baked with leaven" (6:10)
Note: Also requires eating the remainder unleavened in a holy place (6:9), the positive side of the same rule.

Note: Area could also be Festivals and holy days; the provision prescribes the offering itself.

Study record: Offer the prescribed new-moon burnt and sin offerings with their accompaniments
Form basis: "at the new moons you shall bring" (28:11)
Note: Area could also be Festivals and holy days; the provision prescribes the offerings themselves.

Study record: Offer the prescribed Weeks burnt and sin offerings with their accompaniments
Form basis: "you shall bring whole burnt offerings" (28:27)
Note: Area could also be Festivals and holy days; the provision prescribes the offerings themselves.

Study record: Do not profane or break your pledged word
Form basis: "shall not profane his word" (30:3)
Note: Numbers 30:3 both forbids breaking one’s pledged word and requires fulfilling it. The title selects the prohibition as the leading clause. Keeping one’s word is Moral, with Ceremonial overlap for vows to the Lord.

Study record: Apply the stated confirmation or timely annulment rules to a young daughter's vow
Form basis: status rule: "then all her vows shall stand" (30:5)
Note: Numbers 30:4–6 gives the legal effect of the father’s silence or same-day objection. Both outcomes determine the vow’s status. This is a Positive household rule, with Ceremonial overlap because the vow is made to the Lord.

Study record: Apply the stated confirmation, annulment and liability rules to a wife’s vow
Form basis: status rule: "then all her vows shall stand" (30:8)
Note: Numbers 30:7–9 regulates the status of an existing vow on marriage. The linked verses 11–16 address a vow made in the husband’s household and liability for late annulment. Both passages support Positive and Civil with Ceremonial overlap.

Study record: Treat a widow's or divorced woman's vow as binding
Form basis: status: "shall remain against her" (30:10)
Note: Numbers 30:10 makes the widow’s or divorced woman’s vow binding in its own right. The rule directly concerns the force of the vow. The surrounding household rules explain the secondary Civil aspect of her marital status.

Study record: Apply the prescribed purity standard to articles that can or cannot pass through fire
Form basis: "you shall thoroughly purify every covering" (31:20)

Study record: Give the Levites the prescribed towns and surrounding lands in proportion to tribal holdings
Form basis: "give the Levites towns to live in" (35:2)
Note: Land allotment and measurement (Civil) for the landless Levites; their sacred status gives a Ceremonial secondary.

Study record: Set apart the appointed cities of refuge
Form basis: "you shall set apart towns for yourselves" (35:11)

Study record: Do not execute the manslayer before congregational judgment
Form basis: "the killer shall in no wise die before" (35:12)

Study record: Put to death whoever kills with a deadly weapon or in enmity
Form basis: court penalty: "Let the murderer surely be put to death" (35:16)

Study record: The blood-avenger: execute the condemned murderer under the prescribed judgment
Form basis: penalty: "shall himself kill the murderer" (35:19)

Study record: Judge intent and circumstances to distinguish murder from accidental killing
Form basis: "the congregation shall judge between the one" (35:24)

Study record: Congregation: rescue the accidental killer from the avenger of blood
Form basis: "the congregation shall rescue the killer" (35:25)

Study record: Remain in the city of refuge until the high priest dies
Form basis: "he must live in the city of refuge" (35:28)
Note: 35:28 also permits return after the high priest's death and 35:27 frees the avenger from liability outside the city; neither is a prohibition, so not mixed.

Study record: Congregation: return the accidental killer to the city of refuge
Form basis: "restore him to the city of refuge" (35:25)

Study record: Do not accept ransom for a condemned murderer
Form basis: "shall not accept a ransom for a life" (35:31)
Note: 'He shall surely be put to death' restates the murder penalty as the ground of the ban, so the record is not treated as mixed.

Study record: Do not accept ransom to release the manslayer before the high priest's death
Form basis: "You shall not accept a ransom concerning flight" (35:32)

Study record: Do not pollute the land with bloodshed
Form basis: "you shall in no wise stain with murder" (35:33)
Note: Numbers 35:33–34 forbids polluting the land with murder. The prohibition supports Moral, while the homicide judgments in verses 29–32 and atonement provision in verse 33 support Civil. The passage supports both and leaves category priority open.

Study record: An inheriting daughter: marry within the father's clan under the tribal-land provision
Form basis: "they shall marry from their father’s clan" (36:6)
Note: 'Let them marry whom they please' grants freedom within the clan limit; the operative rule is the requirement, so Positive.

Study record: Preserve ancestral tribal allotments against transfer to another tribe
Form basis: "no inheritance … shall pass from tribe to tribe" (36:7)
Note: The title is phrased positively, but the verse's main clause forbids transfer; 'shall hold fast' is its stated ground, not a separate duty.

Study record: Hear disputes and judge Israelites and resident sojourners justly
Form basis: "judge justly between a man and his brother" (1:16)

Study record: Do not show partiality between great and small
Form basis: "You shall not show partiality in judgment" (1:17)
Note: Mixed: also 'you shall judge the small and the great alike' (positive). 613 match N284 (unlearned judge) is Maimonides' reading of this verse; impartiality fits the title.

Study record: Do not fear human pressure in judgment
Form basis: "shall not shrink before the face of man" (1:17)

Study record: Do not add to or take away from the word God commanded
Form basis: "You shall not add unto the word" (4:2)
Note: The closing 'you shall keep the commandments' is a general charge to obey, not a separate operative clause, so not mixed.

Study record: Teach God's words and acts to children and grandchildren
Form basis: "you shall teach your sons" (4:9)
Note: The teaching command is affirmative. Guarding one's memory is a separate direction, and ‘lest you forget’ states the purpose of that direction.

Study record: Do not bow down to or serve the heavenly bodies
Form basis: "lest you … be led astray to bow down" (4:19)

Study record: Love the Lord with heart, soul and strength
Form basis: "you shall love the Lord your God" (6:5)

Study record: Teach children and speak of God’s words throughout ordinary daily life
Form basis: "you shall teach them to your sons" (6:7)

Study record: Write God's words on doorposts and gates
Form basis: "you shall write them upon the doorposts" (6:9)

Study record: Swear by God's name in the prescribed covenant allegiance
Form basis: "you shall swear by His name" (6:13)

Study record: Do not put God to the test
Form basis: "shall not put the Lord … to the test" (6:16)

Study record: Do not intermarry with the specified idolatrous Canaanite peoples
Form basis: "Neither shall you intermarry with them" (7:3)
Note: Deuteronomy 7:1–3 identifies seven nations and prohibits intermarriage with them. The marriage restriction is Civil under the conquest and household rule. Verse 4 makes prevention of idolatry the basis for Moral overlap.

Study record: Do not covet the silver or gold on idols
Form basis: "You shall not covet the silver or gold" (7:25)
Note: Deuteronomy 7:25 expressly forbids coveting the metal on the idols because it can lead Israel to stumble. This provision targets desire for an idolatrous object. The ban on devoted objects in verse 26 supports the Ceremonial overlap.

Study record: Do not take the silver or gold from idols
Form basis: "nor take it unto yourself" (7:25)
Note: Deuteronomy 7:25 separately forbids taking the silver or gold attached to the images. The prohibition addresses a means of idolatrous entanglement. Verse 26 supplies the devoted-object context.

Study record: Do not bring a devoted idolatrous object into your house
Form basis: "shall not bring an abomination into your house" (7:26)
Note: Deuteronomy 7:26 both bars bringing the object inside and commands its rejection. Those clauses regulate the same response to an idol under the ban, so the form is mixed and the explicit household prohibition is primary.

Study record: Bless the Lord after eating and being satisfied in the good land
Form basis: "and bless the Lord your God" (8:10)

Study record: Do not worship the Lord by adopting the nations’ condemned practices
Form basis: "You shall not do so unto the Lord" (12:4)
Note: Deuteronomy 12:4 refers back to the nations’ sites and practices in verses 2–3. Verse 5 points to the chosen sanctuary, while the parallel in verse 31 specifies condemned acts such as child-burning. Both Moral and Ceremonial readings remain relevant to the elliptical verse.

Study record: Bring the prescribed holy gifts and vowed offerings to the Lord’s chosen place
Form basis: "you shall bring thither your whole burnt offerings" (12:6)

Study record: Eat the prescribed sacred meals at God's chosen place with the eligible household and dependants
Form basis: "you shall eat there before the Lord" (12:7)

Study record: Do not make personal preference the rule of covenant worship
Form basis: "You shall not do all that we do" (12:8)

Study record: Do not offer burnt offerings at unauthorized places
Form basis: "you do not offer your whole burnt offerings" (12:13)

Study record: You may slaughter and eat meat locally, clean and unclean alike
Form basis: "you may slaughter and eat flesh" (12:15)
Note: Deuteronomy 12:15 and 20 explicitly authorize ordinary meat consumption, while verses 21–22 describe local slaughter and who may eat. The catalogue’s permission differs in scope from Maimonides’ duties concerning prescribed slaughter and redemption.

Study record: Pour the blood from meat slaughtered for food onto the ground
Form basis: "you shall pour it upon the earth" (12:16)
Note: This entry requires pouring out the blood. The adjacent prohibition on eating it is separately catalogued and explicitly excluded by this record's own context.

Study record: Do not eat the reserved sacred foods in ordinary towns instead of the chosen sanctuary
Form basis: "You may not eat within your cities" (12:17)
Note: Mixed: also 'you shall eat them before the Lord your God' at the chosen place (12:18), matching 613 match P128.

Study record: Do not neglect the Levite
Form basis: "that you do not forsake the Levite" (12:19)
Note: Deuteronomy 12:17–19 places care for the Levite alongside sacred meals and dues. Its instruction to avoid forsaking him throughout life in the land also supports broader moral care. Either emphasis could govern the primary category.

Study record: Do not inquire into other gods' worship in order to imitate it
Form basis: "You shall not inquire after their gods" (12:30)

Study record: Do not heed an enticement to serve other gods, even from a wonder-worker or close relative
Form basis: "you shall not hearken unto the words" (13:4)

Study record: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the prophet who entices Israel into apostasy
Form basis: stated penalty: "that prophet … shall die" (13:6)
Note: Deuteronomy 13:6 states death liability and directs the community to remove the offender. The record covers the Civil sanction, which is Positive under the catalogue’s convention. Maimonides N26 concerns prophesying in the name of other gods.

Study record: Do not spare the proven enticer to idolatry out of personal attachment
Form basis: "neither shall your eye spare him" (13:9)

Study record: Report the secret enticer to idolatry and do not conceal him
Form basis: "You shall surely report him" (13:10)
Note: Deuteronomy 13:9–10 combines the ban on concealing the enticer with the duty to report him. The record names both and leads with the reporting duty. Maimonides N21 indexes the concealment ban, accounting for the form difference.

Study record: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the proven enticer to idolatry
Form basis: court penalty: "they shall stone him with stones" (13:11)
Note: Deuteronomy 13:11 directs the community to stone the proven enticer. The record selects this Civil penalty, classified as Positive, while Maimonides N16 concerns the enticement itself.

Study record: Investigate a city's reported apostasy diligently
Form basis: "you shall inquire and search diligently" (13:15)

Study record: Carry out the prescribed destruction judgment on the proven apostate city
Form basis: court penalty: "you shall surely slay all the inhabitants" (13:16)
Note: Devoting the city to destruction also has a ceremonial (devoted-things) side; Moral is secondary as this is the penalty for apostasy.

Study record: Do not rebuild the condemned apostate city
Form basis: "shall not be built again" (13:17)
Note: Burning the city and its spoil (13:17a) is a separate positive duty; this record is the no-rebuilding clause, so not mixed.

Study record: Do not retain the condemned apostate city's devoted property
Form basis: "nothing … shall cleave to your hand" (13:18)
Note: Deuteronomy 13:13–18 first requires investigation and then prescribes what happens to the condemned city and its spoil. Verse 18 forbids retaining the property under the ban, making Civil primary and its devoted status Ceremonial.

Study record: Do not make a mourning bald patch for the dead
Form basis: "neither shall you make a bald place" (14:1)
Note: Deuteronomy 14:1–2 prohibits a mourning mark as a bodily distinction for all Israel. Signs, vows and dedications fits this specific restriction, consistent with the bodily mourning rule in Leviticus 19:28. Leviticus 21:5 addresses priests specifically.

Study record: You may eat every clean bird
Form basis: "Every clean bird you may eat" (14:11)
Note: Deuteronomy 14:11 expressly permits eating clean birds. Maimonides P150 concerns distinguishing clean birds, while this catalogue entry records the permission granted once the bird is clean.

Study record: Do not eat an animal that dies of itself
Form basis: "shall not eat anything that dies of itself" (14:21)
Note: Giving the carcass to a resident alien or selling it to a foreigner is an allowed outlet, not a separate duty; the milk clause is separate.

Study record: Set aside the annual produce tithe and eat it at the chosen place
Form basis: "You shall surely tithe all the produce" (14:22)

Study record: Use the prescribed silver substitute if distance prevents carrying the festival tithe
Form basis: "then you shall sell them for silver" (14:25)
Note: Deuteronomy 14:24–26 gives a prescribed procedure when the tithe cannot be carried. The household must convert it to silver, take the silver to the chosen place and use it there. The choice concerns what to buy.

Study record: Deposit the third-year produce tithe locally for Levites, resident foreigners, orphans and widows
Form basis: "you shall bring forth all the tithe" (14:28)
Note: Deuteronomy 14:28–29 requires a local deposit and names the vulnerable beneficiaries. This distribution makes Civil primary. Deuteronomy 26:12–13 restates the third-year tithe and calls it holy, supporting Ceremonial overlap.

Study record: Release covered Israelite debts in the seventh year without exacting payment
Form basis: "you shall release every debt of yours" (15:2)
Note: Mixed: also 'you shall not exact it of your brother' (15:2). Ceremonial secondary because 'a release unto the Lord' is proclaimed; 15:3's foreign-debt permission is TL-05-15-03.

Study record: An Israelite creditor may collect a foreigner’s debt during the seventh-year release
Form basis: "Of a foreigner you may exact" (15:3)
Note: The verse says 'may exact', though Maimonides counts it positive (P142); the brother-release clause belongs to C1035.

Study record: Give to the needy without hardening your heart or resenting the gift
Form basis: "shall not withhold the affection of your heart" (15:7)
Note: The title is phrased positively, but 15:7's operative words are prohibitions; the positive duty to give is in 15:8 (C1039).

Study record: Do not close your hand against the needy
Form basis: "neither shall you close your hand" (15:7)

Study record: Lend sufficient help to the needy brother
Form basis: "and shall surely lend him" (15:8)

Study record: Do not refuse help because the debt-release year is near
Form basis: "lest there be a hidden, lawless thought" (15:9)
Note: Deuteronomy 15:9 calls withholding help because release approaches a sinful response toward a needy brother. That refusal is the Moral prohibition. The seven-year debt release is the Civil setting.

Study record: Provide generously for a released Hebrew servant instead of sending them away empty-handed
Form basis: "You shall furnish him generously" (15:14)
Note: Mixed: also 'you shall not send him away empty' (15:13), 613 match N233; the title leads with providing generously.

Study record: Do not work a firstborn calf
Form basis: "shall do no work with your firstborn calf" (15:19)
Note: 'You shall sanctify' (15:19a) is a separate provision, so not mixed.

Study record: Do not shear a firstborn sheep
Form basis: "neither shall you shear the firstborn" (15:19)
Note: 'You shall sanctify' (15:19a) is a separate provision, so not mixed.

Study record: Eat the unblemished firstborn animals yearly at the Lord’s chosen place
Form basis: "You shall eat it before the Lord" (15:20)
Note: The recorded duty is eating the eligible firstborn at the chosen place. The prohibition on sacrificing a blemished animal explains which animals qualify for that meal. The record does not separately impose that prohibition.

Study record: Eat the blemished firstborn locally, clean and unclean alike
Form basis: "You shall eat it within your cities" (15:22)
Note: Deuteronomy 15:21 excludes the blemished firstborn from sacrifice, then verse 22 admits both clean and unclean people to eat it like game. The same comparison in Deuteronomy 12:15, 22 supports Permission for local consumption.

Study record: Observe Passover in the appointed month of new produce
Form basis: "Keep the month … and observe the Passover" (16:1)

Study record: Do not sacrifice the Passover at an unauthorized local site
Form basis: "You may not sacrifice the Passover" (16:5)

Study record: Include the named household members and neighbors in the Feast of Weeks
Form basis: "you shall rejoice before the Lord your God" (16:11)
Note: Including the Levite, sojourner, orphan and widow in the feast gives a Moral secondary (care for the vulnerable).

Study record: Appoint judges and recording officers in Israel’s towns
Form basis: "You shall appoint judges and recording officers" (16:18)
Note: Appointing judges and recording officers is an affirmative duty. The prohibitions in 16:19 regulate the appointed judges' conduct, which is a separate provision from their appointment.

Study record: Do not plant a sacred grove or cultic tree beside God's altar
Form basis: "shall not plant for yourself a sacred grove" (16:21)
Note: Deuteronomy 16:21 names a sacred grove and any tree beside God’s altar. The cultic object supports Moral and the altar-specific restriction supports Ceremonial. The phrase’s breadth leaves the priority of those categories open.

Study record: Stone the man or woman proven to have served other gods
Form basis: court penalty: "you shall stone them with stones" (17:5)
Note: Mixed: 17:6 forbids execution on one witness ('he shall not die upon the testimony of one witness'); 17:4 also requires diligent inquiry.

Study record: Refer cases too difficult for local judgment to the appointed priests and judge
Form basis: "you shall arise and go up" (17:8)
Note: Deuteronomy 17:8–9 describes referral of disputed judgments and names both the priests and the judge as adjudicators. The chosen venue and priestly participants coexist with a Civil procedure. The site’s application label describes covenant scope.

Study record: Follow the ruling of the appointed priests and judge without turning aside
Form basis: "you shall do according to the matter" (17:10)
Note: Mixed: also 'you shall not turn aside from the word which they declare' (17:11), 613 match N312.

Study record: Apply the prescribed death judgment to presumptuous defiance of the appointed priest or judge
Form basis: court penalty: "that man shall die" (17:12)

Study record: Appoint the ruler the Lord chooses from among Israel’s own people
Form basis: "you shall surely set over yourself a ruler" (17:15)
Note: Mixed: also 'you may not set a foreign man over yourself' (17:15), 613 match N362.

Study record: Ruler: do not multiply horses for yourself
Form basis: "he shall not multiply horses unto himself" (17:16)

Study record: Ruler: do not return the people to Egypt to obtain horses
Form basis: "neither shall he cause the people to return" (17:16)

Study record: Israel: do not return to Egypt by the prohibited way
Form basis: "You shall not return by this way again" (17:16)

Study record: Ruler: do not multiply wives for yourself
Form basis: "he shall not multiply wives unto himself" (17:17)
Note: Kingship rule (Civil); the stated danger that 'his heart turn aside' from God gives a Moral secondary.

Study record: Ruler: do not multiply silver and gold for yourself
Form basis: "he shall not greatly multiply silver and gold" (17:17)

Study record: Ruler: write the prescribed copy of the law from the priests' text
Form basis: "he shall write for himself this second law" (17:18)

Study record: Ruler: read the law throughout your life
Form basis: "he shall read therein all the days" (17:19)
Note: Kingship duty (Civil); its stated aims, to fear the Lord, keep his commandments and not exalt himself, give a Moral secondary.

Study record: Give the priest the foreleg, cheeks and stomach of sacrifices
Form basis: "they shall give unto the priest the foreleg" (18:3)

Study record: Give the priest the first of your sheep's fleece
Form basis: "you shall give unto him" (18:4)

Study record: Allow the eligible incoming Levite to minister at the chosen place
Form basis: "then he shall minister in the name" (18:7)
Note: Deuteronomy 18:6–8 leaves the decision to come to the Levite. On arrival he is entitled to minister alongside the other Levites and receive his allotted share. The record selects that established status and so is Positive.

Study record: Give that ministering Levite his equal allotted share
Form basis: "He shall eat an allotted portion" (18:8)

Study record: Do not interpret the prohibited spoken omens
Form basis: "There shall not be found … interprets spoken omens" (18:10)

Study record: Do not practice sorcery
Form basis: "There shall not be found … works sorcery" (18:10)

Study record: Do not practise divination
Form basis: "There shall not be found … practises divination" (18:10)

Study record: Do not purify a son or daughter by fire
Form basis: "There shall not be found … purifies his son" (18:10)
Note: Deuteronomy 18:9–14 forbids the fire rite on children alongside divination and sorcery as condemned practices. Moral fits that prohibition under the rubric, and the site’s application label identifies the covenant audience.

Study record: Do not chant the prohibited spells
Form basis: prohibited practice: "or chants spells" (18:11)
Note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list of forbidden practices this verse continues.

Study record: Do not practice as a medium
Form basis: prohibited practice: "or is a medium" (18:11)
Note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list of forbidden practices this verse continues.

Study record: Do not practice the prohibited portent-reading
Form basis: prohibited practice: "or observes portents" (18:11)
Note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list this verse continues. 613 match N9 names the Hebrew yidoni; the Saints Translation reads 'observes portents'.

Study record: Do not inquire of the dead
Form basis: prohibited practice: "or inquires of the dead" (18:11)
Note: The negation sits in 18:10, whose list of forbidden practices this verse continues.

Study record: Heed the prophet whom God raises up and who speaks His words
Form basis: "you shall hearken unto him" (18:15)
Note: Deuteronomy 18:15 commands Israel to heed the prophet God raises. Verses 18–19 connect the duty to God’s own words. This supports a Positive moral duty, while the site’s fulfillment label concerns the identity or application of the prophet.

Study record: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the presumptuous false prophet
Form basis: stated penalty: "that prophet shall die" (18:20)
Note: Deuteronomy 18:20 gives the legal consequence for presumptuous prophecy. Verses 21–22 give the community a test and tell it not to spare the false prophet. The Positive Civil sanction differs from Maimonides’ prohibitions N26 and N27.

Study record: Do not spare the prophet whose claimed divine prediction proves false
Form basis: "you shall not spare him" (18:22)

Study record: Add three more refuge cities when God enlarges your borders
Form basis: "you shall add three cities more" (19:9)

Study record: Do not spare the intentional murderer from the prescribed judgment
Form basis: "Your eye shall not spare him" (19:13)
Note: Mixed: also 'you shall cleanse the guilt of innocent blood from Israel' (19:13), the positive aim of carrying out the judgment.

Study record: Do not remove your neighbour's established boundary
Form basis: "You shall not remove your neighbour’s boundaries" (19:14)
Note: The brief lists boundaries as Civil; moving a neighbour's marker is also theft, hence Moral secondary.

Study record: Establish charges on two or three witnesses; one witness is insufficient
Form basis: "two witnesses ... shall every matter be established" (19:15)
Note: The verse states both the insufficiency of one witness and the two- or three-witness threshold. The catalogue records the full Civil evidence rule, with the affirmative threshold first. Maimonides N288 counts the prohibition separately.

Study record: Impose the intended penalty on a proven malicious witness
Form basis: court penalty: "do unto him as he wickedly purposed" (19:19)
Note: Mixed: also 'Your eye shall not spare him' (19:21), forbidding leniency in applying the penalty.

Study record: Israel: do not fear the enemy in the prescribed war
Form basis: "you shall not fear them" (20:1)
Note: The prohibition applies when Israel goes to battle against a superior force. God’s presence supplies the reason for courage. Military conduct falls under Civil in this rubric, and the site’s covenant-specific label describes its scope.

Study record: Honor the prescribed exemptions from battle for a house, vineyard, betrothal or fear
Form basis: "the scribes shall speak unto the people" (20:5)
Note: The scribes must announce the exemptions; for the exempted man 'Let him go' works as a permission, but the record frames the duty to honour them.

Study record: Offer the specified distant city peace before besieging it
Form basis: "call ... forth with an offer of peace" (20:10)

Study record: Place the distant city that accepts peace under the prescribed tribute and service
Form basis: status: "shall pay you tribute, and be subject" (20:11)

Study record: Apply the stated judgment to the males of the conquered distant city
Form basis: "you shall slay every male therein" (20:13)

Study record: Preserve the stated women and dependants from that judgment
Form basis: exception: "save the women and the dependent households" (20:14)
Note: The exception expressly places women and dependent households outside the preceding killing order. Positive records the protected legal status the force must observe.

Study record: Take and use the permitted spoil of the specified distant city
Form basis: "you shall take as spoil unto yourself" (20:14)
Note: The spoil is given to Israel for its use in the distant-city case. The recorded provision grants an entitlement to take and consume it. The surrounding orders concern the conduct of war, which fits Civil.

Study record: Apply the devotion judgment to the seven named nations
Form basis: "you shall utterly devote them to destruction" (20:17)
Note: The main command orders Israel to carry out a conquest judgment, so Civil is primary. Its form of devotion supports the ceremonial overlap. The separate no-survivor clause is in verse 16.

Study record: Do not destroy food-producing trees for siegeworks
Form basis: "you shall not destroy its trees" (20:19)
Note: 20:20 adds permissions ('you may destroy' trees bearing no fruit); permissions are not requirements, so not mixed.

Study record: Release the captive wife if the husband no longer desires her
Form basis: "you shall send her forth free" (21:14)
Note: The verse's other clauses (no sale, no contempt) are separate records C1114 and C1115, so not mixed.

Study record: Do not sell the released captive wife
Form basis: "she shall not be sold for silver" (21:14)
Note: Selling her would treat a freed woman as property, a wrong in itself, hence Moral secondary.

Study record: Do not treat the released captive wife with contempt
Form basis: "You shall not treat her with contempt" (21:14)
Note: The operative clause forbids degrading the released woman because the husband has humbled her. That is a direct duty toward her. The captive-marriage statute supplies the Civil setting, and Maimonides N264 specifies enslavement.

Study record: Do not displace the actual firstborn in favor of the loved wife's son
Form basis: "he may not make ... the firstborn" (21:16)

Study record: Give the actual firstborn his prescribed double inheritance portion
Form basis: "he shall acknowledge the firstborn" (21:17)

Study record: Apply the prescribed death judgment in the established rebellious-son case
Form basis: court penalty: "the men of his city shall stone him" (21:21)

Study record: Bury an executed person the same day rather than leave the body hanging overnight
Form basis: "you shall surely bury him that day" (21:23)
Note: The same-day burial duty and overnight exposure ban are explicit Civil rules about an executed person’s body. The final clause warns against defiling the land. Whether that gives the burial rule a second category of Ritual purity remains an editorial judgment.

Study record: Return your fellow Israelite’s lost animal or property
Form basis: "you shall surely bring them back" (22:1)
Note: Mixed: also 'You shall not see ... and disregard them' (22:1) and 'you may not disregard it' (22:3), per N269.

Study record: Safeguard found property while its owner is unknown or absent
Form basis: "you shall gather them into your house" (22:2)

Study record: A woman: do not wear the prohibited man's equipment
Form basis: "A woman shall not have a man’s equipment" (22:5)
Note: The prohibition on a woman having a man’s equipment is explicit. The verse calls the conduct an abomination and gives no further rationale. Moral remains the working label, while a covenant-separation reading remains possible.

Study record: A man: do not wear the prohibited woman's robe
Form basis: "neither shall a man put on" (22:5)
Note: The prohibition on a man wearing a woman’s robe is explicit. The same abomination clause addresses both prohibitions and gives no further rationale. Moral remains the working label, while a covenant-separation reading remains possible.

Study record: Release the mother bird if taking her young or eggs
Form basis: "You shall surely let the mother go" (22:7)
Note: The passage both requires releasing the mother and forbids taking her with the young. It permits taking the young and promises well-being. The text leaves the reason for the restriction open, so Civil resource regulation and a Moral duty toward the animal remain possible readings.

Study record: Build a protective parapet on a new house's roof
Form basis: "you shall make a parapet for your roof" (22:8)
Note: The Saints text makes avoidance of bloodshed the purpose of the parapet requirement. Maimonides separately derives a broader prohibition against leaving hazards from this wording, which is distinct from this record's affirmative roofing duty.

Study record: Do not sow your vineyard with a different crop
Form basis: "You shall not sow your vineyard" (22:9)

Study record: Mixed vineyard seed and yield become consecrated
Form basis: status rule: "become consecrated" (22:9)
Note: The record addresses the consequence of mixed sowing: both products acquire consecrated status. Positive describes that legal status. Maimonides N216 formulates the resulting restriction on benefiting from the produce.

Study record: Do not plough with an ox and donkey yoked together
Form basis: "You shall not plough" (22:10)
Note: This is the middle of three rules against mixing kinds in 22:9–11. The rubric treats mixed yoking as Ceremonial separation. The agricultural subject explains the site’s civil and land label.

Study record: Elders: discipline the husband proved to have falsely accused his wife
Form basis: court penalty: "shall take that man and chasten him" (22:18)

Study record: Fine the false-accusing husband the prescribed amount payable to the woman's father
Form basis: court penalty: "they shall fine him a hundred shekels" (22:19)

Study record: The husband proved to have falsely accused his wife: do not divorce her
Form basis: "he may not put her away" (22:19)
Note: Mixed: also 'she shall be his wife' (P219), the duty to keep her as wife.

Study record: Apply the prescribed judgment when the stated premarital sexual accusation is established
Form basis: court penalty: "the men of her city shall stone her" (22:21)

Study record: Apply the prescribed judgment in the stated consensual betrothal violation
Form basis: court penalty: "they shall be stoned with stones" (22:24)

Study record: Apply the prescribed death judgment to the man who forces the betrothed woman
Form basis: court penalty: "you shall put to death only the man" (22:25)

Study record: Do not punish the woman assaulted in the stated circumstances
Form basis: "unto the young woman you shall do nothing" (22:26)
Note: Not punishing the coerced victim is a court rule (Civil) resting on justice to the innocent, hence Moral secondary.

Study record: In the stated assault on an unbetrothed virgin, require the prescribed payment to her father
Form basis: penalty payment: "shall give unto the father ... fifty silver didrachmas" (22:29)

Study record: Apply the stated marriage obligation in the unbetrothed-virgin case
Form basis: "she shall be his wife" (22:29)
Note: Marriage obligation imposed as a consequence of the violation (Civil), with Moral secondary as the underlying act is a sexual wrong.

Study record: The man in the stated unbetrothed-virgin case: do not divorce her
Form basis: "he may not put her away" (22:29)

Study record: Observe the stated assembly restriction concerning the specified genital injuries
Form basis: "shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:2)
Note: The verse sets eligibility for entry into Israel’s assembly. The restriction concerns membership status, which supports Civil under the rubric. Aquinas understands public standing and Maimonides applies the rule to marriage eligibility.
Adjudication: Independent category audit · Scripture review resolved

Study record: Observe the stated assembly restriction concerning the specified parentage
Form basis: "shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:3)
Note: The Saints reading makes specified parentage a disqualification for assembly membership. Civil captures that eligibility rule, while the narrower rabbinic legal definition belongs to Maimonides’ marriage interpretation.
Adjudication: Independent category audit · Scripture review resolved

Study record: Observe the stated assembly restriction concerning Ammonites and Moabites
Form basis: "shall not enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:4)
Note: The provision sets an ancestry-based restriction on admission. Nehemiah 13:1–3 invokes this law when separating people from Israel. That community-membership setting supports Civil, alongside Maimonides’ marriage-law reading.
Adjudication: Independent category audit · Scripture review resolved

Study record: Do not seek the specified Ammonite and Moabite peace or advantage
Form basis: "You shall not speak peace unto them" (23:7)
Note: National policy toward Ammon and Moab (war and government), so Civil.

Study record: Do not abhor the Edomite
Form basis: "You shall not abhor an Edomite" (23:8)
Note: Kinship is the reason given for the direct ban on abhorring an Edomite. Moral describes that duty, and the next verse’s third-generation admission rule explains the Civil overlap and Maimonides’ use.
Adjudication: Independent category audit · Scripture review resolved

Study record: Do not abhor the Egyptian
Form basis: "you shall not abhor an Egyptian" (23:8)
Note: Israel’s past residence in Egypt is the reason given for the direct ban on abhorring an Egyptian. Moral describes that duty, and the third-generation admission rule supplies its Civil context.
Adjudication: Independent category audit · Scripture review resolved

Study record: Admit the stated third-generation descendants of Edomites and Egyptians to the assembly
Form basis: status: "shall enter the assembly of the Lord" (23:9)
Note: The passage affirmatively establishes eligibility in the third generation. Civil fits assembly membership. Maimonides N54 and N55 express the corresponding marriage rule as a prohibition on rejection.
Adjudication: Independent category audit · Scripture review resolved

Study record: Keep the military camp from evil and indecency
Form basis: "you shall keep yourself from every evil thing" (23:10)
Note: The wording requires active vigilance while encamped against enemies, so Positive follows the operative clause. Military discipline is Civil. The surrounding rules say the camp must be holy because the Lord walks in it.

Study record: Leave the military camp when unclean from the stated discharge and return only after purification
Form basis: "he shall go forth outside the camp" (23:11)
Note: The verse requires leaving and washing and expressly forbids entering while unclean. The record covers the complete purity procedure. Maimonides N78 isolates the entry ban.

Study record: Set apart a place outside the military camp for excretion
Form basis: "you shall have a place outside the camp" (23:13)
Note: Camp hygiene, which the brief lists as Civil; the passage's holiness motive (23:15) lies outside this verse.

Study record: Do not return the escaped slave to his master
Form basis: "You shall not deliver unto his master" (23:16)
Note: Asylum rule for escaped slaves (Civil); shielding the fugitive from his master is also mercy to the oppressed, hence Moral secondary.

Study record: Allow the escaped slave to settle in the place he chooses among you
Form basis: status: "He shall dwell with you" (23:17)
Note: The verse grants the escaped person a choice of residence. The record addresses Israel as host, which must respect that choice. This is a Positive asylum obligation with an ethical protection for the vulnerable.

Study record: Do not afflict the escaped slave
Form basis: "You shall not afflict him" (23:17)
Note: The record isolates the direct prohibition on afflicting the escaped person, parallel to the ban on oppressing a resident foreigner in Exodus 22:20. The asylum and settlement rules give the prohibition its Civil setting.

Study record: Do not practice the prohibited prostitution
Form basis: "There shall be no prostitute" (23:18)

Study record: Do not perform or receive the prohibited initiation rites
Form basis: "no woman who performs initiation rites" (23:18)
Note: The Saints reading explicitly prohibits the initiation practices for women and men. The operative rule is a ban on participation, which the rubric treats as Moral. The site label captures its covenant setting.

Study record: Do not bring a prostitute's hire as a sanctuary vow offering
Form basis: "shall not bring the hire of a prostitute" (23:19)

Study record: Do not bring the stated price of a dog as a sanctuary vow offering
Form basis: "not bring ... nor the price of a dog" (23:19)

Study record: A foreigner may be charged interest
Form basis: "Unto a foreigner you may lend at interest" (23:21)
Note: The Saints Translation says a lender may charge a foreigner interest. The next clause expressly prohibits charging a fellow Israelite. Permission describes the former clause, while Maimonides P198 enumerates an affirmative command.

Study record: Do not delay to pay a vow to God
Form basis: "you shall not delay to pay it" (23:22)
Note: Vow law (Ceremonial); keeping one's word to God also has a moral core (cf. Eccl 5:4–5), hence Moral secondary.

Study record: Pick a neighbor’s standing grain by hand without using a sickle
Form basis: "you may gather heads of grain" (23:25)
Note: Permission ('you may gather') limited by 'you shall not put a sickle' (a ban, not a requirement, so not mixed). 613 matches P201/N267 apply it to hired workers.

Study record: Eat grapes in a neighbor’s vineyard without gathering them in a vessel
Form basis: "you may eat grapes" (23:26)
Note: Permission ('you may eat grapes') limited by 'you shall put none in a vessel' (a ban, not a requirement, so not mixed). 613 matches P201/N268 apply it to hired workers.

Study record: Do not remarry a divorced former wife after her intervening marriage
Form basis: "former husband ... may not take her again" (24:4)
Note: The conditional case culminates in a specific remarriage ban, so Negative and Civil are clear. The text associates it with defilement and an abomination. The secondary Moral category depends on how that rationale is read.

Study record: Exempt the newly married man from war and other imposed duty for one year
Form basis: "he shall not go forth unto war" (24:5)
Note: The title says 'exempt', but the verse's operative words forbid sending him to war or laying duty on him (N311), so Negative.

Study record: Newly married husband: gladden your wife during the prescribed year at home
Form basis: "shall gladden his wife whom he has taken" (24:5)
Note: This record concerns the husband’s affirmative duty to gladden his wife. The one-year public-duty exemption is the Civil setting and has its own catalogue entry at C1167.

Study record: Do not take the livelihood-sustaining mill or millstone in pledge
Form basis: "You shall not take a mill ... in pledge" (24:6)
Note: Pledge law (Civil); 'takes a life in pledge' grounds it in mercy to the debtor, hence Moral secondary.

Study record: Do not enter the debtor's house to seize a pledge
Form basis: "you shall not enter his house" (24:10)

Study record: Pay the worker's wages at the prescribed time
Form basis: "same day you shall pay his wages" (24:15)
Note: The passage forbids withholding wages and orders same-day payment. It calls failure a sin against the needy worker, making Moral primary. Civil captures the enforceable timing rule. Both clauses are in the recorded provision.

Study record: Do not execute parents for children's sins or children for parents' sins
Form basis: "Fathers shall not die for children" (24:16)
Note: 613 match N287 is the rabbinic reading (no testimony from relatives); the plain verse bars executing one person for another's sin. Same negative form.

Study record: Do not take the widow's garment in pledge
Form basis: "neither shall you take a widow’s garment" (24:17)
Note: Pledge law (Civil) protecting the widow, whose care is a moral duty, hence Moral secondary.

Study record: Do not pervert the judgment of the sojourner, orphan or widow
Form basis: "You shall not pervert the judgment" (24:17)
Note: Justice for the vulnerable as a duty (Moral; cf. Deut 27:19); it concerns judgment in court, hence Civil secondary.

Study record: Do not return for a forgotten harvest sheaf
Form basis: "you shall not return to take it" (24:19)
Note: Mixed: also 'It shall be for the poor...' (P122), assigning the forgotten sheaf to the poor.

Study record: Do not glean the remaining olives after the first gathering
Form basis: "you shall not return to glean what remains" (24:20)
Note: Mixed: also 'It shall be for the sojourner...', assigning what remains to the poor.

Study record: Give lashes under judicial supervision in proportion to the offense, with a maximum of forty
Form basis: court penalty: "they shall scourge him before them" (25:2)
Note: Mixed: also 'shall not add thereto' (25:3; N300), the forty-stripe limit.

Study record: Do not muzzle the ox while it threshes
Form basis: "You shall not muzzle an ox" (25:4)
Note: The verse sets a rule for threshing, so Civil describes its immediate operation. Moral captures the concern for the working animal and the principle Paul applies to workers’ support in 1 Corinthians 9:8–10.

Study record: The childless widow in the stated levirate case: do not marry outside the prescribed kinship
Form basis: "shall not be married outside unto a man" (25:5)

Study record: The surviving brother in the stated levirate case: undertake the prescribed marriage duty
Form basis: "Her husband’s brother shall go in unto her" (25:5)

Study record: Establish the child of the levirate marriage in the deceased brother's name
Form basis: status rule: "established in the name of the dead" (25:6)

Study record: Apply the prescribed household designation after the levirate refusal
Form basis: status rule: "his name shall be called in Israel" (25:10)
Note: Public designation imposed after the levirate refusal; a status consequence, so Positive.

Study record: Apply the prescribed penalty in the stated genital-seizure case
Form basis: court penalty: "you shall cut off her hand" (25:12)
Note: Mixed: also 'your eye shall not spare her' (N293). P247 (rescuing the pursued) is the rabbinic reading; the verse states a penalty.

Study record: Do not keep differing sets of weights or measures
Form basis: "You shall not have ... differing weights" (25:13)

Study record: Do not accept payment to kill an innocent person
Form basis: curse: "Cursed is he who takes a bribe" (27:25)
Note: Curse formula read as a prohibition; the people's 'So be it' is the covenant-ceremony response, not a separate standing provision.
